skills_considered.reason: The discovery ledger is a research surface another batch owns; this wave's question is patient provenance and counting, so findings are proposed through commit candidates instead of ledger edits.
No source in this group tests a therapy against a mechanism; forging hypotheses from single-patient drug histories would manufacture a lead.
No compound is proposed as a candidate; anti-seizure medication histories in case reports are clinical descriptions, not molecules for BLOCK-1 triage.
Scientists do not touch the four current files; changes are proposed as commit candidates for a later BATCH_COMMIT.
No proposed change narrows or reverses a consolidated baseline claim; the triples are published in the candidates for an auditor to run.

group_assessment.weighting: PubMed counts 2026-10-03: Spagnoli C[au] 140 records, 1 intersecting WWOX (this review). A child neurology group writing a PRISMA review; every WWOX datum is secondary and comes from one cohort paper.

field_density.note: Thirteen PubMed records pair WWOX with movement disorder; this review is the one that states a WWOX-specific neonatal hypokinetic phenotype.

multihop.note: All 74 references enumerated; the only WWOX reference is ref 46, Piard 2019. Its six genotype lines in Table S1 were matched to Piard Supplemental Table 1 patients 1, 2, 3, 4, 9 and 11, whose 'Movement disorder' and 'Poor spontaneous movements' rows were read.

corpus_crossquery.note: No record names the review. The theme 'hypokine' reaches PAPER 145 and LIT-0442 (the 2026 L239R case report) and PAPER 013.

entries.proposition: The review states that an early-onset hypokinetic movement disorder occurs only with WWOX variants, citing one source.
entries.snippet: Only in patients with WWOX gene variants there is an associated early onset hypokinetic MD with little or no psychomotor development from birth [46].

entries.proposition: The WWOX section is built from 5 of 20 cases of a single cited cohort.
entries.snippet: WWOX (WW domain-containing oxidoreductase): 5/20 cases had neonatal-onset epilepsy with associated MD.

entries.proposition: The hypokinetic description is 'very limited spontaneous movements', attributed to reference 46.
entries.snippet: MD is strikingly hypokinetic with very limited spontaneous movements, while upper limbs’ dystonia, myoclonus, startles, paroxysmal involuntary movements, and episodes of boxing/pedaling were also described [46].

entries.proposition: The discussion turns the observation into a diagnostic suggestion.
entries.snippet: neonatal-onset hypokinetic MD appears exceptional and highly suggestive for WWOX-related disorders.

entries.proposition: The authors themselves name a recognition bias in favour of hyperkinetic disorders.
entries.snippet: However, as hyperkinetic MD might be easier to recognize, a potential bias cannot be completely excluded.

entries.proposition: Table S1 counts hypokinesia in five WWOX patients.
